To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strong coupling spectrum of N = 2 SU(2) pure Yang-Mills is composed of only two particles: the magnetic monopole (of mass m = 4) and the dyon (of unit charge and mass m = 2).

the strong-couping spectrum of N = 2 SUSY pure YM theory is given by the two particles that are responsible for the singular behavior of the solution of Seiberg-Witton, and the weak coupling spectrum is the same as the strong coupling one, with the addition of an infinite tower of massive BPS states.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the global structure of N=2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory in four dimensions.
the global structure of Seiberg-Witen theory and its BPS states, in particular in the strong coupling region.
the global properties of the solution of N = 2 SU(2) Yang-Mills theory, and the spectrum of stable and unstable BPS states in both the weak- and strong-coupling regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spectrum is the same in weak- and strong-coupling, with the same mass formula, but the BPS states are different: in the weak-coupled region, there are the usual massive states, but in strong-coupling there are only the two singularities.

the spectrum of BPS states is given by a pair of massless particles (the photon and the neutral dyon) and two massive particles (the magnetic monpole and the dyon with unit electric charge) in the weak-couping region, and by the latter two only in the strong-coupilng region.

the SeibergWitten theory is not a theory of magnetic monopoles and dyons, but rather a theory of two particles, the monopole and dyon of unit charge, which are present in both the weak- and strong-coupling regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Seiberg- Witten solution is the exact solution of the N=2 Yang-Mills theory in the strong-cupling region.
we have found the spectrum of BPS states of the Seib erg-Witten theory in the whole range of the moduli space.
we show that in the N = 1 supersymmetric pure Yang–Mills theory the BPS states are stable in a very simple way.

, in order to obtain the strong-coupled spectrum, it is not necessary to know the weak-coupled one, nor to use semiclassical methods.

the Seiberg–Witten theory, which was initially developed to solve the N = 1 supersymmetric Yang–Mills theory in the weak-couping region, is also a very useful tool in studying the strong-couplig region of the N =  2 supersymmetric Yang– Mills theory.
